note.text:
Water-borne diseases are prevented by keeping germs out of water and food:
• Treat drinking water: boil it (rolling boil for at least one minute), filter it, or add chlorine (water-treatment tablets or a few drops of bleach as instructed).
• Store treated water in clean, covered containers and use a clean cup or tap to take it out.
• Use latrines or toilets; never defecate near streams or wells; keep latrines away from water sources.
• Wash hands with soap and water after using the toilet and before cooking or eating.
• Wash fruits and vegetables with clean water; cook food well; cover food from flies.
• Protect wells and springs; clear stagnant water; do not bathe or wade in streams where bilharzia is common.
• Vaccination is available for some (cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A).

worked_example.problem: Give three ways that {v} can reduce water-borne diseases.
steps: Build latrines away from the stream so faeces do not reach it.
Boil or chlorinate drinking water and store it covered.
Wash hands with soap after the toilet and before eating.
worked_example.answer: Latrines away from the stream, treated and covered water, handwashing with soap.

example: Store it covered, in a clean container.

pick.r: Flies carry germs from faeces to food.

pick.q: Which method makes water safe by killing germs with a chemical?
e: Cloth removes dirt, not all germs.

questions.prompt: Put the steps for making stream water safe to drink in order.

items.text: Fetch the water in a clean container
Let it settle and filter it through a clean cloth
Boil it for at least one minute
Let it cool with the lid on
Store it covered and pour it out with a clean cup

pick.q: When should you wash your hands with soap?
pick.r: after using the toilet and before eating or cooking
e: Before eating is just as important.
Soap removes germs that water alone leaves.
pick.y: These are the key times to remove germs.

right.text: Latrines should be far from wells.
